stimulus.text:
The engraving shows armed farmers fleeing through a village street in Springfield, Massachusetts, as uniformed troops with a cannon advance behind them. The farmers, many carrying muskets, run past bare winter trees and a white house. The artist's signature, “C. Kendrick,” appears at the lower right.
— C. Kendrick, Shays's forces fleeing troops at Springfield, c. 1902 (from a 1902 publication)

stem: The engraving best illustrates which feature of Shays's Rebellion?

options.text: The rebels won control of the Springfield armory
options.misconception: The rebels failed to take the armory; the troops in the engraving are driving them off.

options.text: The rebellion was put down by force raised outside the national government
The rebels were mostly merchants from Boston
options.misconception: Background: the rebels were farmers from western Massachusetts, not Boston merchants.

options.text: The rebellion ended when Congress sent the Continental Army into Massachusetts
options.misconception: Background: Congress had no army to send; the force came from Massachusetts itself.

rationales.B: Background from the books: the rebellion was put down by a Massachusetts militia of nearly 4,000 men, raised by the governor and paid for by Boston merchants, because Congress had no troops to send.
rationales.A: The engraving shows the rebels fleeing, not holding the armory they tried to seize.
rationales.C: Background: the rebels were western Massachusetts farmers facing taxes and foreclosures, not Boston merchants.
rationales.D: Background: Congress under the Articles could not raise an army, so no federal force was sent.
rationales.general:
1. Read the image. Armed farmers flee while uniformed troops with a cannon advance.
2. Background: the troops were a Massachusetts militia, raised by the governor.
3. Background: Congress had no army of its own to send to Springfield.
4. The force that ended the rebellion came from the state, not from the nation.
Remember: the picture shows a state solving by force what the nation could not touch.
